symptom: On a fresh database volume, backend startup stops first because transactions does not exist and then because Goals.category_id is incompatible with categories.category_id.
evidence: Researcher-supplied TypeORM/MySQL errors plus source inspection showing migrationsRun=true, synchronize=false, no earlier core-table migration, and signed/unsigned entity drift.

root_cause.summary: The migration chain altered core tables before creating them, and category/user foreign-key columns did not consistently match their unsigned referenced primary keys.

actions_attempted: Recorded and received explicit researcher approval for the exact UC-07 schema proposal.
Added an earlier idempotent core-table initialization migration and aligned approved entity metadata and receipt DTO mappings.
Passed targeted backend ESLint, repository backend ESLint, and the Nest production build.
Attempted to locate Docker on Windows and through WSL without deleting or resetting any volume.
commands_rerun: Docker CLI discovery on Windows and WSL
reusable_resolution: With Docker Compose v2 available, run the approved stack on the fresh volume and confirm every migration completes, the backend becomes healthy, and /api/health returns HTTP 200.
prevention: Every fresh-volume migration chain must create referenced core tables before alter/index migrations and must use identical signedness on both sides of each MySQL foreign key.
